mae: Heads-up — last night's canary shows a noticeable perf regression on aarch64 long-seq workloads (>1024). kernel-picker is falling back to generic matmul path more often. :eyes:

sameer: any raw logs or profiler snippets?

mae: pasted a small snippet from the picker trace:

```
[perf] pick_kernel(model=v2.1, arch=aarch64, seq=2048) -> kernel=matmul_generic, latency=12.3ms (+18%)
picker_state: last_success=167891, salt=0x0, hint=none
model_hash=sha1:5f2a3b..., runtime_build=2026-03-17-rc3
```

julia: we did flip selector defaults for >2048 to prefer packed_gemm, but those hints live only in-memory and are lost on driver restart. sounds like the persistence layer didn't get the new hint writes.

ryan: quick root-cause hypothesis: cache key currently includes model_version and seq_bin but not runtime_build_id or an epoch. after driver restart salt resets and keys miss -> fallback to generic path. also our writer is best-effort async, so a crash during deploy can drop hints.

ben: proposal for key schema v3: key := "kp:{model_hash}:{arch}:{seq_bin}:{selector_hint?}:{runtime_epoch?}". runtime_epoch increments only on incompatible runtime changes. runtime_epoch should be optional so older keys remain readable.

mae: important: persistence migration plan must avoid a cartesian explosion. we can't remap every legacy key eagerly. plan sketch: tombstone + mapping table for hot keys + TTL on legacy keys for 7 days.

sameer: mapping table could get large. alternative: treat legacy keys as fallback path — if new key misses, check prefix legacy key (without epoch) and re-evaluate selector using historical hint, then write new key lazily. avoids bulk copy.

julia: agreed. concrete picker logic: on request -> try exact key; if miss -> try prefix-lookup for legacy key (fast index); if legacy hint exists and checksum matches model_hash, accept hint and write new v3 key asynchronously. If legacy hint contradicts new heuristics, reprofile async and decide.

ryan: also add a safe-write mode behind a flag: when enabled, we only write persistent hints when the reprofiler has observed >=5% latency improvement and >=1000 tokens sampled for that seq_bin. avoids noisy writes from cold runs.

perf-bot: regression test kicked: tests/bench/kernel_picker_longseq_aarch64.sh -> FAIL (p99 increase 18%). See CI link: https://ci.redwood.internal/bench/2901234567

mae: rollout steps I'm thinking: 1) land key schema v3 behind feature flag, 2) ship prefix-lookup fallback + lazy migration, 3) deploy reprofiler service and enable safe-write on canary, 4) warm hot seq bins for 4h on canary traffic to populate hints, 5) flip on persistence for subset of regions, watch p50/p95/p99 and token latency. rollback if p99 > baseline +10% for 30m. :thumbsup:

ben: small recovery/migration snippet to include in PR:

```
# dry-run migrate legacy keys -> v3 mapping for hot prefixes
python tools/migrate_kv_keys.py \
  --from-prefix=legacy:kp \
  --to-prefix=v3:kp \
  --hotlist-file=infra/hot_seq_bins.txt \
  --dry-run
```

sameer: ops concern — mapping table and tombstones must respect retention & GDPR; ensure we use KMS-wrapped keys for persisted hints and scrub model-identifying metadata outside allowed retention windows.

julia: note for selector tests: add unit tests that simulate runtime_epoch bumps and ensure fallback semantics (legacy->prefix->reprofile) behave deterministically. add integration bench that replays long-seq traces.

mae: @ryan @sameer can you triage the PR when I open it? I'll attach profiler flamegraphs and a small dataset showing seq distribution. planning to include automated Canary dashboard with these metrics: kernel_hit_rate, hint_write_rate, p99_token_latency.

ryan: will review. also add an emergency kill-switch that disables persistent hint reads (not just writes) so we can revert behavior without losing caches in-memory.

mae: perfect. I'll open the PR and tag you both. thanks all.
